FIX FOUR FOLLOW-UP REVIEW FINDINGS ON PR #802. Target branch codex/run-38040971079-1, expected head 7134d82; fail closed and write nothing if it moved. Only .github/workflows/container-image-parity.yml, scripts/dev/review_lab/lifecycle.py, tests/test_review_lab_v3.py, tests/test_container_image_parity.py and CHANGES.md may change.

F1 (P2, parity workflow ~line 67 and the duplicate helper): GNU timeout waits after SIGTERM unless --kill-after is given, so a stalled pull can exceed the 120 s bound. CHANGE both helpers to `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=10 120 docker pull --quiet "${image}"`; assert the exact string in tests/test_container_image_parity.py.

F2 (P3, CHANGES.md:28): the entry says five attempts; the policy is three. CHANGE the wording to three attempts (and 60 s/120 s per attempt as implemented).

F3 (P2, lifecycle.py ~line 304): pull_review_images() pulls both compose images before _review_api_base_image() can reject a missing/forbidden API base. CHANGE: resolve and validate the API base image FIRST (before any pull), then pull postgres, redis, base. Update the ordering test and make the forbidden-base test assert that NO docker command at all ran (neither `docker pull` nor `docker compose pull`).

F4 (P2, parity workflow ~line 158): with 4 images x 3 x 120 s the pre-pull can take over 24 minutes, leaving too little of the 40-minute parity job for the web build and serialized compose builds. CHANGE: raise the 'Built image parity' job timeout-minutes to 55 and update its budget comment (4 images x 3 attempts x 120 s + kill-after + sleeps ≈ 25 min, plus the previous 30-minute build budget); update the test assertion.
